issues: Header uses <button> elements with onClick that set window.location.href for navigation, so navigation links are not rendered as <a> elements; tests expect links with role "link" for Services, Training, About, Contact, causing failures (e.g., m1-header-footer.test.tsx). Change navLinks to use <Link> or <a> with href for each navigation item.

Header navigation for mobile collapses correctly but the <button> elements for Services, Training, Contact are not accessible links; replace them with <Link> components or <a> elements and ensure they have the accessible name matching the page (e.g., "Services").

Header missing proper ARIA attributes for the menu button to meet contrast requirements and color contrast fails for button-primary (foreground #ffffff on #1f8a8a does not meet 4.5:1 contrast). Adjust button styles to meet WCAG AA contrast, e.g., use a darker teal for background or a darker text color.
Responsive layout fails: page width exceeds viewport (410px on 390px). Ensure container elements use max-width: 100% and appropriate padding/margins to prevent horizontal overflow.

Wordmark SVG provides only aria-label but no visible text; tests look for a link with name "The Bayes Group" which is present, but the link text is not the visible wordmark, causing duplicate name issues in header/footer. Ensure the wordmark link renders accessible text and does not duplicate link names across header/footer, or adjust tests accordingly. However spec requires both header and footer navigation, so keep separate but ensure each link is uniquely identifiable via role "link" and name "Services" etc.
Footer navigation links are correct, but the footer wordmark is not a link; tests expect a non‑link wordmark, which is fine. No change needed there.
Home page hero button "Explore services" has class "button-secondary" but tests look for a link with name "Explore services"; ensure it renders as <Link> with appropriate accessible name.
Contact form success handling clears fields but the test checks that fetch is not called; ensure no fetch is invoked at all (e.g., remove any default form action).

Training page filter buttons are rendered as <button> with correct aria-pressed, but the test expects visibility filtering; ensure the filter logic correctly hides non‑matching course cards (currently may not hide, causing visibility test failures).
feedback: Many acceptance tests fail because navigation elements are rendered as buttons instead of links, causing the test suite to not find the expected accessible link roles. Fix the Header (and any other navigation) to use <Link> components for navigation items, ensure proper ARIA attributes, contrast compliance, and responsive layout without overflow. Also adjust button styling for contrast and verify the training filter visibility logic. After these changes the tests should pass.
